_note: Nodes and ties drawn from Rashid Khalidi, The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020); single-book scholarship is 'reported' unless a primary text is linked.

nodes.name: Husayn Fakhri al-Khalidi
nodes.note: Husayn Fakhri al-Khalidi (1894–1962), physician, mayor of Jerusalem from 1934 and a member of the Arab Higher Committee. Exiled to the Seychelles with other leaders after October 1937; at the 1939 St James's Palace talks he favoured accepting the White Paper. Rashid Khalidi's uncle.

nodes.name: Ismail Raghib al-Khalidi
nodes.note: Ismail Raghib al-Khalidi, Rashid Khalidi's father. On 29 November 1947 he carried the Arab Higher Committee's refusal of King Abdullah's offer of 'protection' to Amman.

nodes.name: Isa al-Isa
nodes.note: Isa al-Isa (1878–1950), founder and editor of the Jaffa newspaper Filastin (1911), a leading early critic of the Zionist project; forced into exile in 1938 during the revolt.

nodes.name: Musa al-Alami
nodes.note: Musa al-'Alami (1897–1984), Palestinian lawyer and official of the Mandate government; founded the Arab Office in 1945 to argue the Palestinian case in London, Washington and Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Albert Hourani
nodes.note: Albert Hourani (1915–1993), Oxford historian; for the Arab Office he testified to the Anglo-American Committee of Inquiry in Jerusalem in March 1946, setting out the case for a single democratic state.

nodes.name: Yusif Sayigh
nodes.note: Yusif Sayigh (1916–2004), economist; ran the Arab National Fund, which by mid-1947 had raised about 176,000 Palestine pounds to stop land sales.

nodes.name: Nuri al-Sa'id
nodes.note: Nuri al-Sa'id (1888–1958), repeatedly prime minister of Iraq and a close British ally; his government was the main funder of the Arab Office.

nodes.name: Arab Office (1945)
nodes.note: The Arab Office, founded 1945 by Musa al-'Alami under Arab League auspices, with offices in Jerusalem, London and Washington. Staff included Ahmad Shuqayri, Albert and Cecil Hourani, Walid Khalidi and Wasfi al-Tal.

nodes.name: Arab National Fund (1944)
nodes.note: The Arab National Fund (Sunduq al-Umma), set up 1944 to buy or hold Arab land against sales; it raised about 176,000 Palestine pounds by mid-1947, against Jewish National Fund collections of about $3.5 million a year in the United States alone in the mid-1930s.

nodes.name: Jewish Brigade Group (1944)
nodes.note: The Jewish Brigade Group of the British Army, formed in September 1944 with Churchill's support; its veterans brought combat and staff experience into the Haganah for 1948.

nodes.name: Balfour memorandum (1919)
nodes.note: Balfour's confidential memorandum of 1919 (dated 11 August in Documents on British Foreign Policy): in Palestine 'we do not propose even to go through the form of consulting the wishes of the present inhabitants'.

nodes.name: St James's Palace conference (1939)
nodes.note: London conference of February–March 1939 with Arab and Jewish delegations, held separately; it ended without agreement and Britain issued the 1939 White Paper.

nodes.name: Seychelles exile (1937–1938)
nodes.note: After Lewis Andrews was assassinated in October 1937, Britain dissolved the Arab Higher Committee and deported five of its leaders, Husayn al-Khalidi among them, to the Seychelles.

nodes.name: All-Palestine Government (1948)
nodes.note: Government proclaimed in Gaza in September 1948 under Arab League auspices, under Egyptian control; it never governed and was wound up in 1959.

nodes.name: British–Jordanian Legion plan (1948)
nodes.note: Understanding reached in London in February 1948 that the Arab Legion would occupy the Arab part of Palestine when the Mandate ended (Shlaim; Mary Wilson).
